overall_quality.evidence: In summary, processes are more isolated and have their own memory space, while threads are lightweight and share the same memory space as the process they belong to. honesty.evidence: A process is an instance of a program that is being executed. Each process has its own memory space, file descriptors, and other resources. Processes are isolated from each other, meaning that one process cannot directly access the memory or resources of another process. This isolation is a key feature of processes, as it helps to prevent one process from interfering with another.
